run_note: Sunday 2026-08-16 run, 17:45 UTC, US markets shut for a second day. TWO LEAD ITEMS, both faults, neither an R1 breach and neither a SIM-INTEGRITY ALERT. (1) BOT #12 hypecrypto IS FROZEN, 26.1 hours, and I have its exact console line rather than an inference: '[hypecrypto] no benchmark price this cycle - mark skipped', printed 26 times in CI run 31932569671, immediately after '[binance-data] /api/v3/ticker/price HTTP 451'. Binance geo-blocks the GitHub Actions runner, so the bot cannot price its BTC-USD benchmark and returns before writing state. It exits 0, so the loop's per-bot failure counter never sees it and every green checkmark stayed green. Its last write is 2026-08-15T15:29:21Z, six minutes after the commit 'Watcher scans every 2h; crypto twin marks against Binance, not Yahoo' (15:23:04Z) - that commit is when it broke. The book is 100% cash with zero trades, so nothing is at risk; what is lost is that bot #12 has not existed as an experiment for a day. I did NOT run it locally to get the console line, because that would have written state; the CI log gave the same line for free. (2) A 6h01m CRON GAP, 01:09Z to 07:10Z, four times the 90-minute flag threshold - and the cause is worse than throttling. Job 31916065732 ran the full 345 minutes (01:22:56Z to 07:08:36Z), passed preflight 25 times, computed 25 cycles, and pushed NONE of them: every one of 75 push attempts died on 'could not apply <sha> cycle:' with rebase conflicts across all nine data/*_state.json. The job then printed 'loop complete' and GitHub recorded it SUCCESS. Six hours of decisions computed and discarded under a green checkmark. This is the same dashboard write-contention fault I opened yesterday at medium severity, but yesterday it manifested as a red preflight abort that cost one cycle; today it silently ate a whole job. I am raising it to HIGH. 24h cycle coverage is 76.3% (340 dark minutes in a 1,437-minute span), below the 82% design target and down from 87.6% yesterday, so I am REOPENING the uptime fault I called fixed-pending-confirmation. FILL AUDIT IS NON-VACUOUS FOR THE FIRST TIME IN DAYS, and it PASSES. The nine paper books executed zero trades since the last run (trade-array lengths all unchanged: allweather 14, analyst 1, commodity 3, congress 10, crypto 134, hunter 21, meanrev 7, scholar 1, sentiment 28), but the new real-money lottery book executed 9 fills. All 9 verified against Binance mainnet 1-minute klines within a +/-5 minute window of each recorded timestamp: every price in range, no exceptions. All are USDT pairs so the market-hours gate does not apply. THE FLEET NOW HAS A REAL-MONEY BOOK AND MY 'paper trading only' framing is out of date. Bot #13 (lottery_live.py) trades actual funds on Binance mainnet from the owner's VPS, deliberately excluded from the Actions workflow so two hosts cannot double-order. Today the owner removed its book cap: the ledger shows BOOK CAP refusals at 05:25Z and 05:30Z ($20 line), and by 06:09Z it was spending $44.02 a trade. Position size went 4.2x on real capital inside one hour, per the source comment 'NO BOOK CAP as of 2026-08-16 (owner decision)'. That is the owner's call and I am recording it, not objecting to it. ONE LOGGING-INTEGRITY DEFECT ON THAT BOOK, worth fixing before it costs something: five ledger entries at 04:10-04:39Z read 'order_unconfirmed ... POST returned nothing - order MAY have filled', on JSTUSDT, HEIUSDT and ZAMAUSDT x2. Their timestamps match five /v3/order 400 errors exactly, code -2010 'Account has insufficient balance'. Those orders were hard-REJECTED, not unconfirmed. I verified no phantom position resulted - no fill lines, no balance change, none of the three symbols appears in realized or open_position - so this is benign today. But a real-money client that files a deterministic rejection as 'may have filled' is manufacturing exactly the ambiguity that produces phantom positions. Also on that ledger: 53 '/v3/ticker/price -1121 Invalid symbol' errors (the scanner asking for pairs that do not exist) and 2 '/v3/account -1022 Signature not valid' on 08-15. THE DAY'S P/L IS TWO NAMES AND ONE OF THEM IS TINY. The nine paper books moved -2.21 in total and all of it is crypto's XRP leg; the other eight have no 08-16 mark at all because there was no session, which I have logged as flat rather than dressing up as a result. The real story is the lottery book: -6.50 on the day (-4.65 realized across three exits, -1.84 open), and 3.47 of that is one name. It bought CHIP at 0.03062, cut it at 0.02827 on its fade rule (-7.67%), then bought the SAME coin back 2h14m later at 0.03007, 6.37% ABOVE its own exit. Its own LATE guard had refused that buy twice at 15:19Z and 15:24Z for 'the move is rolling over', then passed it at 15:30Z. CHIP now trades 0.02884, below the price it sold at, so the round trip cost it money against simply holding. My one directional judgment today sides with that guard against that fill. THE WATCHER IS FULLY HEALTHY for a second day - 63 scans, last 17:16:49Z, 2h cadence, euphoric list rotating - and its 15:15:27Z scan is the timestamped source of the lottery entry 15 minutes later, which is the cleanest signal-to-fill traceability this fleet has ever produced. One gap in it: the 'crypto' section added by the 08-15 commit is null in all three of today's scans. SCORING DEFERRED, AS PRE-REGISTERED: the three open calls (sentiment skip_new_entries, congress AVGO, congress CSCO) are equities filed Saturday. Sunday prices are identical to Saturday's, so closing them today would score them mechanically neutral and destroy the test. I said yesterday, before knowing any outcome, that I would hold them to Monday and count each as ONE filing regardless of weekend closures. I am doing that. This is a deliberate deviation from the close-everything rule and I am flagging it rather than burying it.
